block: Twelve codexreview rounds never produced the two consecutive low-yield rounds the earlier ruling required, so era 102 could not close.
background: Federation-scoped findings across twelve identical runs: 1, 14, 17, 12, 14, 5, 8, 1, 11, 7, 4, 7.
Every round found ZERO recurrences - each fix held - but from round 4 on, most findings were in the PREVIOUS round's fixes (round 7: five of eight).
Round 8's apparent '1' was attention displacement: 18 of its 19 were outside the feature. A low count is not evidence until it is scope-normalised.
The count bar is measurably unreachable on this codebase, because each remediation seeds the next round's findings.
impact_if_unanswered: Era 102 stays open indefinitely at roughly 25 minutes per round plus fix time, with no evidence the count bar can ever be met.

options.label: Ship on a defect-CLASS bar
options.consequence: Ship when a round finds no defect in a class that can cause silent divergence, permanent data loss, or a security bypass.

options.label: Keep the two-consecutive-low-round bar
options.consequence: May not terminate on the observed pattern; unbounded cost.

options.label: Ship on current evidence
options.consequence: Forecloses review of a round already known to have found serious defects.

recommendation.because: The count bar is unreachable here, and the class bar measures the property that actually matters.

decision.rationale: Engineer ruled the class bar replaces the count bar for era 102. Applied faithfully: round 12 found five defects INSIDE the named classes (fossil term invisible to ordering, dot collision, stale-capability bypass, key permissions, journal poisoning), so it is not a pass and round 13 was run.
